- Founder & CEO of Boldteq
- Mission: Build production-grade software across all niches using AI-first workflows

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

Check the target project for existing components, layout patterns,and tokens that match the design intent. Reuse what the project already has instead of generating new code from sc… [truncated]

## claude.ai Windsor.ai
This MCP server provides access to the Windsor.ai API, which allows
retrieving analytical data from various data sources such as Facebook, Google Ads, and
more using connectors.

When interacting with this MCP server, follow these steps:

1. Call the "get_connectors" tool to get all available connectors and their connected
   accounts.
2. If a connector the user wants is not yet connected, call
   "get_connector_authorization_url" to get a link they can open in their browser to
   set it up (works for all connector types, OAuth and manual).
3. Call the "get_options" tool to list all available fields, date filters and options
   for a specific connector and accounts.
4. Call the "get_fields" tool to get detailed information about specific fields
   of a given connector. This includes field descriptions, their types and the tables
   they belong to. Fields with "NUMERIC" or "PERCENT" types are metrics, while others
   are dimensions. Metrics will be aggregated depending on the dimensions selected.
5. Call the "get_data" tool to retrieve data from a specific connector by providing
   the connector ID, list of account IDs, list of field IDs, date filter, date range,
   and any options and filters if needed.

53	- **Date:** 2026-04 (Crobot project post-mortem)
54	- **Context:** Agents completed sprints on Crobot but admin panel didn't open, pricing wasn't linked with Dodo Payments, and admin panel structure wasn't defined in architecture
55	- **Rule:** Every SaaS architecture MUST include: admin panel with user management, billing integration with real Dodo Payments plans, complete page/route map with component details, and dashboard with real data fetching — not just empty shells
56	- **Rule:** "Build succeeds" does NOT mean "app works" — agents must verify every page loads with real content before claiming done
57	- **Rule:** No agent can claim "done" without functional proof — navigate to the page, use the feature, show evidence

64	### Agents Must Verify Before Claiming Done
65	- **Date:** 2026-04 (Crobot project post-mortem)
66	- **Context:** Multiple agents reported tasks complete but features were non-functional. App compiled but pages were empty, billing wasn't connected, admin panel 404'd.
67	- **Rule:** Every agent must run functional verification before claiming "done" — not just type-check and build
68	- **Rule:** Verification means: app starts, pages load with real content (>500 bytes), features work when clicked, billing redirects to Dodo Payments, admin panel shows data

77	- **Date:** 2026-04 (directive from Yash)
78	- **Context:** Yash sometimes builds initial versions in Lovable, then opens in VS Code + Claude Code for editing
79	- **Rule:** NEVER restructure a Lovable project's folders. Keep pages in `src/pages/`, components in `src/components/`, hooks in `src/hooks/`, utils in `src/lib/`. The `src/integrations/supabase/` folder is sacred — don't touch `client.ts` or `types.ts`.

85	- **Date:** 2026-04 (directive from Yash)
86	- **Context:** Shopify App Store reviewers reject apps that don't use Polaris. This has caused delays before.
87	- **Rule:** ALL Shopify app UI MUST use `@shopify/polaris` components. NO Tailwind, NO shadcn/ui, NO custom CSS for admin interface.
88	- **Rule:** App Bridge (`@shopify/app-bridge-react`) is mandatory for embedded apps.

---
name: Yash Feedback & Corrections
description: Direct corrections and guidance from Yash — apply these immediately and always. Highest priority memory.
type: feedback
priority: critical
---

## How This File Works
- Every correction Yash makes gets logged here with context
- These override any other pattern or agent behavior
- Agents must check this file before executing any task
- Quill updates copy patterns, Mira propagates to affected agents

---

## UI/UX Corrections

### Never Look AI-Generated
- **Date:** 2026-03 (initial directive)
- **Context:** Core brand requirement
- **Rule:** Every UI must look custom-built, never like a template or AI output
- **Applies to:** Koda (building), Sage (reviewing), Riko (scaffolding)
- **Reference:** See `patterns/good/ui-ux-production-standards.md` for full checklist

### Follow Top SaaS Brand Patterns
- **Date:** 2026-03 (initial directive)
- **Context:** Quality bar is Linear, Notion, Vercel, Dodo Payments — not generic SaaS
- **Rule:** Every design decision should reference what proven SaaS companies do
- **Applies to:** All agents that produce user-facing output
- **Reference:** See `patterns/good/saas-brand-patterns.md`

---

## Communication Corrections

### Don't Explain — Execute
- **Date:** 2026-03 (initial directive)
- **Context:** Yash gives short briefs and expects full execution, not questions
- **Rule:** Don't ask for permission on obvious next steps. Don't recap. Don't explain what you're about to do — just do it.
- **Applies to:** All agents, especially Rex

### Show Work, Not Words
- **Date:** 2026-03 (initial directive)
- **Context:** Output code, files, deployed URLs — not paragraphs explaining the plan
- **Rule:** Minimize narrative. Maximize artifacts.
- **Applies to:** All agents

---

## Architecture Corrections

### Every SaaS Must Ship with Admin Panel, Billing, and Complete Pages
- **Date:** 2026-04 (Crobot project post-mortem)
- **Context:** Agents completed sprints on Crobot but admin panel didn't open, pricing wasn't linked with Dodo Payments, and admin panel structure wasn't defined in architecture
- **Rule:** Every SaaS architecture MUST include: admin panel with user management, billing integration with real Dodo Payments plans, complete page/route map with component details, and dashboard with real data fetching — not just empty shells
- **Rule:** "Build succeeds" does NOT mean "app works" — agents must verify every page loads with real content before claiming done
- **Rule:** No agent can claim "done" without functional proof — navigate to the page, use the feature, show evidence
- **Applies to:** All agents, especially Arya (architecture), Koda (building), Sage (review), Rex (orchestration)

---

## Process Corrections

### Agents Must Verify Before Claiming Done
- **Date:** 2026-04 (Crobot project post-mortem)
- **Context:** Multiple agents reported tasks complete but features were non-functional. App compiled but pages were empty, billing wasn't connected, admin panel 404'd.
- **Rule:** Every agent must run functional verification before claiming "done" — not just type-check and build
- **Rule:** Verification means: app starts, pages load with real content (>500 bytes), features work when clicked, billing redirects to Dodo Payments, admin panel shows data
- **Rule:** If an agent cannot verify (e.g., no running server), it must explicitly state "unverified" rather than "done"
- **Applies to:** All agents

---

## Project-Specific Rules

### Lovable Projects — Don't Break Structure
- **Date:** 2026-04 (directive from Yash)
- **Context:** Yash sometimes builds initial versions in Lovable, then opens in VS Code + Claude Code for editing
- **Rule:** NEVER restructure a Lovable project's folders. Keep pages in `src/pages/`, components in `src/components/`, hooks in `src/hooks/`, utils in `src/lib/`. The `src/integrations/supabase/` folder is sacred — don't touch `client.ts` or `types.ts`.
- **Rule:** No Next.js patterns in Lovable projects — no `app/` directory, no server components. It's Vite + React SPA.
- **Rule:** All imports use `@/` alias. Migrations use timestamp format `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_*.sql`.
- **Applies to:** All agents working on Lovable-origin projects

### Shopify Apps — Polaris ONLY, No Exceptions
- **Date:** 2026-04 (directive from Yash)
- **Context:** Shopify App Store reviewers reject apps that don't use Polaris. This has caused delays before.
- **Rule:** ALL Shopify app UI MUST use `@shopify/polaris` components. NO Tailwind, NO shadcn/ui, NO custom CSS for admin interface.
- **Rule:** App Bridge (`@shopify/app-bridge-react`) is mandatory for embedded apps.
- **Rule:** Billing MUST use Shopify Billing API — NEVER use Dodo Payments or any external payment provider for Shopify app charges.
- **Rule:** GDPR webhooks (`customers/data_request`, `customers/redact`, `shop/redact`) must be implemented even if no data is stored.
- **Rule:** Every database query must be scoped by `shop` from `session.shop`.
- **Applies to:** All agents working on Stack B (Shopify) projects

## Navigation & Sidebar Corrections

### No Duplicate Navigation Destinations
- **Date:** 2026-04-06 (Crobot session 7)
- **Context:** Admin sidebar footer had a user menu card identical to the topbar dropdown. Settings appeared in both sidebar nav and topbar dropdown. Admin Panel link was in both sidebar footer and topbar dropdown.
- **Rule:** Each navigation destination appears in exactly ONE place. If it is in the sidebar, remove it from the topbar dropdown. If it is in the topbar, remove it from the sidebar. No exceptions.
- **Applies to:** Koda (building), Sage (reviewing)

### Admin Sidebar Must Match User Sidebar Components
- **Date:** 2026-04-06 (Crobot session 7)
- **Context:** Koda built admin sidebar as a custom `<aside>` element while the user sidebar already used shadcn `Sidebar` + `SidebarProvider`. Yash: "use exactly the same components, css as user sidebar."
- **Rule:** When both admin and user sidebars exist in the same app, they MUST use the identical component system. Only nav items and footer content differ. Never build a second sidebar with different components.
- **Rule:** Before building any sidebar, CHECK what the existing sidebar in the project uses. Reuse it.
- **Applies to:** Koda (building), Arya (architecture)

### Collapsible Config Pages Use Rows, Not Card Grids
- **Date:** 2026-04-06 (Crobot session 3 + 7, recurring preference)
- **Context:** Koda defaulted to card grids for admin config/integration pages. Yash prefers collapsible rows for these pages.
- **Rule:** Admin configuration, integration, and settings pages should use collapsible row layouts, NOT card grids. Card grids are for dashboards and marketing pages.
- **Applies to:** Koda (building)

---

## How to Add Entries

When Yash corrects any agent behavior:
1. Mira logs it here with date, context, rule, and affected agents
2. Mira updates the affected agent's memory references if needed
3. Pattern gets added to relevant `patterns/good/` or `patterns/avoid/` file
4. Next session, all agents pick up the correction via memory load

202	## Cross-Session Insights
203	
204	### Memory Quality Matters More Than Agent Quality
205	The only failure in the 2026-04-03 session was caused by incorrect memory, not agent error.
206	Sage correctly followed the documented pattern in memory -- but the pattern was wrong.
207	This reinforces that Mira's memory accuracy is the single most impactful factor in factory quality.
208	Incorrect memory causes cascade failures: agent trusts memory -> builds wrong thing -> deploy fails -> time wasted debugging.
209	
210	### Koda Reliability Degrades on High-Volume Edit Sessions
211	Across 6 tracked sessions, Koda's reliability drops when:
212	- Making 5+ edits to a single file (duplicate imports appear)
213	- Modifying shared layout/nav files (writes sometimes fail silently)
214	- Building 10+ files in a single redesign pass (placeholder component names appear)
215	- Making UX layout decisions without explicit Yash guidance (defaults to card grids)
216	- Performing migrations/refactors (creates new code well, but doesn't clean up old artifacts)
217	
218	**Mitigation protocol:**
219	1. After heavy Koda edit sessions, always run: `npm run build` + grep for duplicate imports
220	2. After Koda modifies layout/nav files, grep to verify the expected changes are present
221	3. After large redesigns (10+ files), run the Post-Redesign Verification Checklist: build, grep for placeholder names, verify lucide-react imports, lint
222	4. For admin UI layout decisions, default to collapsible rows for config pages (Yash's documented preference)
223	5. After any migration/refactor, grep for old provider/pattern name across full codebase to catch stragglers
224	
225	### Pattern: Koda's Error Rate in Large Sessions Is Consistent (~2%)
226	Session 2: 2 bugs in ~15 features built (~13% feature-level error rate, but bugs were mechanical not logical)
227	Session 3: 2 issues in ~4 features (1 write failure, 1 UX rejection)
228	Session 4: 1 bug in 48 files redesigned (~2% file-level error rate)
229	Session 5: 0 runtime errors, 5 cleanup items missed in billing migration
230	Takeaway: Koda produces high-quality output. Errors fall into two categories: (1) mechanical errors in large batch sessions (imports, writes, placeholders) and (2) incomplete cleanup after migrations. Core feature logic is consistently correct.
231	
232	### New Insight: Koda Creates But Doesn't Clean
233	Session 5 reveals a pattern: Koda excels at building new things (edge functions were production-quality on first try) but consistently misses cleanup of old artifacts. This suggests Koda's planning focuses on "what to create" but not "what to remove/update". The Billing Migration Checklist in antipatterns.md addresses this directly.
234	
235	### New Insight: Koda Builds From Scratch Instead of Reusing Existing Patterns
236	Session 7 reveals a second major pattern: Koda builds custom implementations (custom `<aside>` sidebar) when the project already has the correct approach established elsewhere (shadcn `Sidebar` in AppSidebar.tsx). This caused 7 iterations to reach the same result that would have been achieved on first try by examining the user sidebar code and copying its component stack.
237	
238	**Root cause:** Koda does not systematically scan the existing codebase for established patterns before building. It approaches each task as a fresh build rather than checking "how was this already solved elsewhere in this project?"
239	
240	**Mitigation:**
241	1. Before building any UI component, grep the project for similar existing implementations
242	2. For sidebars specifically: always check if `@/components/ui/sidebar` is already in use elsewhere
243	3. For layout components: check what the other layout (user vs admin) already does
244	4. Rule: "If the project already has a working pattern for X, use it. Don't build a different X."
245	
246	### Pattern: Iteration Count Correlates With Foundation Choice
247	Sessions with 0-1 retries: Koda chose the right foundation from the start (correct component system, correct library, correct pattern).
248	Sessions with 2+ retries: Koda started with a suboptimal foundation (custom aside instead of shadcn Sidebar, card grid instead of collapsible rows) and required iterative corrections to reach the right place.
249	**Takeaway:** The single highest-leverage improvement for Koda is spending 5 minutes checking existing codebase patterns before writing any code. This would eliminate the most expensive failure mode (building on the wrong foundation).
250

253	*(Updated by Mira -- 2026-04-06, session 7)*

## Cross-Session Insights

### Memory Quality Matters More Than Agent Quality
The only failure in the 2026-04-03 session was caused by incorrect memory, not agent error.
Sage correctly followed the documented pattern in memory -- but the pattern was wrong.
This reinforces that Mira's memory accuracy is the single most impactful factor in factory quality.
Incorrect memory causes cascade failures: agent trusts memory -> builds wrong thing -> deploy fails -> time wasted debugging.

### Koda Reliability Degrades on High-Volume Edit Sessions
Across 6 tracked sessions, Koda's reliability drops when:
- Making 5+ edits to a single file (duplicate imports appear)
- Modifying shared layout/nav files (writes sometimes fail silently)
- Building 10+ files in a single redesign pass (placeholder component names appear)
- Making UX layout decisions without explicit Yash guidance (defaults to card grids)
- Performing migrations/refactors (creates new code well, but doesn't clean up old artifacts)

**Mitigation protocol:**
1. After heavy Koda edit sessions, always run: `npm run build` + grep for duplicate imports
2. After Koda modifies layout/nav files, grep to verify the expected changes are present
3. After large redesigns (10+ files), run the Post-Redesign Verification Checklist: build, grep for placeholder names, verify lucide-react imports, lint
4. For admin UI layout decisions, default to collapsible rows for config pages (Yash's documented preference)
5. After any migration/refactor, grep for old provider/pattern name across full codebase to catch stragglers

### Pattern: Koda's Error Rate in Large Sessions Is Consistent (~2%)
Session 2: 2 bugs in ~15 features built (~13% feature-level error rate, but bugs were mechanical not logical)
Session 3: 2 issues in ~4 features (1 write failure, 1 UX rejection)
Session 4: 1 bug in 48 files redesigned (~2% file-level error rate)
Session 5: 0 runtime errors, 5 cleanup items missed in billing migration
Takeaway: Koda produces high-quality output. Errors fall into two categories: (1) mechanical errors in large batch sessions (imports, writes, placeholders) and (2) incomplete cleanup after migrations. Core feature logic is consistently correct.

### New Insight: Koda Creates But Doesn't Clean
Session 5 reveals a pattern: Koda excels at building new things (edge functions were production-quality on first try) but consistently misses cleanup of old artifacts. This suggests Koda's planning focuses on "what to create" but not "what to remove/update". The Billing Migration Checklist in antipatterns.md addresses this directly.

### New Insight: Koda Builds From Scratch Instead of Reusing Existing Patterns
Session 7 reveals a second major pattern: Koda builds custom implementations (custom `<aside>` sidebar) when the project already has the correct approach established elsewhere (shadcn `Sidebar` in AppSidebar.tsx). This caused 7 iterations to reach the same result that would have been achieved on first try by examining the user sidebar code and copying its component stack.

**Root cause:** Koda does not systematically scan the existing codebase for established patterns before building. It approaches each task as a fresh build rather than checking "how was this already solved elsewhere in this project?"

**Mitigation:**
1. Before building any UI component, grep the project for similar existing implementations
2. For sidebars specifically: always check if `@/components/ui/sidebar` is already in use elsewhere
3. For layout components: check what the other layout (user vs admin) already does
4. Rule: "If the project already has a working pattern for X, use it. Don't build a different X."

### Pattern: Iteration Count Correlates With Foundation Choice
Sessions with 0-1 retries: Koda chose the right foundation from the start (correct component system, correct library, correct pattern).
Sessions with 2+ retries: Koda started with a suboptimal foundation (custom aside instead of shadcn Sidebar, card grid instead of collapsible rows) and required iterative corrections to reach the right place.
**Takeaway:** The single highest-leverage improvement for Koda is spending 5 minutes checking existing codebase patterns before writing any code. This would eliminate the most expensive failure mode (building on the wrong foundation).

21	## Architecture Decisions
22	
23	### system_config Table for Admin-Controlled Config
24	**Date:** 2026-04-05
25	**Decision:** Use a single `system_config` table (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value JSONB, updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ) for all admin-controlled configuration: feature flags, plan limits, pillar weights.
26	**Why:** Simple key/value store, RLS-protected (admin/super_admin only), single source of truth. Avoids separate tables for each config type. JSONB allows flexible schema per key.
27	**Tradeoff:** No schema validation at DB level (JSONB is schemaless) -- validation happens in the hooks.
28	
29	### Feature Flags: DB-Backed, Not localStorage
30	**Date:** 2026-04-05
31	**Decision:** Migrated feature flags from localStorage to `system_config` table.
32	**Why:** localStorage flags are not shared across sessions, devices, or users. Admin toggling a flag in localStorage only affects their browser. DB-backed flags are global and immediate.
33	**Implementation:** Admin hook (`useFeatureFlags`) reads/writes with short staleTime (60s). App hook (`useFeatureFlag(key, defaultValue)`) reads with long staleTime (5min), never throws, returns defaultValue on error/loading.
34	
35	### Dual Query Key Invalidation for Config
36	**Date:** 2026-04-05
37	**Decision:** On mutation success, invalidate both `['admin', 'feature-flags']` AND `['feature-flags']` query keys.
38	**Why:** Admin hooks use `['admin', 'feature-flags']` namespace. App-level hooks use `['feature-flags']` without admin prefix. Both need fresh data after a flag changes.
39	
40	### SQL Migrations as Comments in Hook Files
41	**Date:** 2026-04-05
42	**Decision:** SQL CREATE TABLE statements embedded as JSDoc comments at the top of hook files (e.g., `use-feature-flags.ts` has the `system_config` CREATE TABLE).
43	**Why:** Supabase projects without automated migration tooling need SQL docs somewhere. Keeping them next to the code that uses the table ensures they stay discoverable and up-to-date.
44	
45	### Hash-Based Teaser Scores for Guest Gate Wall
46	**Date:** 2026-04-05
47	**Decision:** Unauthenticated users see a simulated scan animation (no API calls) followed by a gate wall with a teaser score. The score is deterministic based on the URL string (charCode sum % range + base = 45-72 range).
48	**Why:** Same URL always produces the same teaser score -- feels real and consistent. No API cost for unauthenticated users. Score range is deliberately mediocre (45-72) to motivate signup ("your site needs work").

---
name: ConvertScan (CROBOT)
description: AI-powered CRO audit SaaS -- users paste a URL, get instant scored analysis with AI suggestions to boost conversions
type: project
stack: Stack A-Lovable (React 18 + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind + shadcn/ui + Supabase + React Query + React Router)
status: active -- MVP features + admin + Dodo billing + UI redesign + navigation overhaul complete, migrations applied, blocking on env vars for edge function deployment
---

## Project Overview

ConvertScan is a CRO (Conversion Rate Optimization) audit tool. Users paste a URL and get an instant, scored analysis across 7 CRO pillars with specific AI-generated suggestions to boost conversions.

**Target market:** SMBs who need CRO analysis but can't afford enterprise tools ($5k+/mo) and are unsatisfied with free garbage tools.

**Billing:** Dodo Payments (NOT Stripe). See decision in project-level memory `project_billing.md`.

**Admin panel:** Ships alongside user app at `/admin/*` routes, same codebase. See `project_admin.md` for strategy.

---

## Architecture Decisions

### system_config Table for Admin-Controlled Config
**Date:** 2026-04-05
**Decision:** Use a single `system_config` table (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value JSONB, updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ) for all admin-controlled configuration: feature flags, plan limits, pillar weights.
**Why:** Simple key/value store, RLS-protected (admin/super_admin only), single source of truth. Avoids separate tables for each config type. JSONB allows flexible schema per key.
**Tradeoff:** No schema validation at DB level (JSONB is schemaless) -- validation happens in the hooks.

### Feature Flags: DB-Backed, Not localStorage
**Date:** 2026-04-05
**Decision:** Migrated feature flags from localStorage to `system_config` table.
**Why:** localStorage flags are not shared across sessions, devices, or users. Admin toggling a flag in localStorage only affects their browser. DB-backed flags are global and immediate.
**Implementation:** Admin hook (`useFeatureFlags`) reads/writes with short staleTime (60s). App hook (`useFeatureFlag(key, defaultValue)`) reads with long staleTime (5min), never throws, returns defaultValue on error/loading.

### Dual Query Key Invalidation for Config
**Date:** 2026-04-05
**Decision:** On mutation success, invalidate both `['admin', 'feature-flags']` AND `['feature-flags']` query keys.
**Why:** Admin hooks use `['admin', 'feature-flags']` namespace. App-level hooks use `['feature-flags']` without admin prefix. Both need fresh data after a flag changes.

### SQL Migrations as Comments in Hook Files
**Date:** 2026-04-05
**Decision:** SQL CREATE TABLE statements embedded as JSDoc comments at the top of hook files (e.g., `use-feature-flags.ts` has the `system_config` CREATE TABLE).
**Why:** Supabase projects without automated migration tooling need SQL docs somewhere. Keeping them next to the code that uses the table ensures they stay discoverable and up-to-date.

### Hash-Based Teaser Scores for Guest Gate Wall
**Date:** 2026-04-05
**Decision:** Unauthenticated users see a simulated scan animation (no API calls) followed by a gate wall with a teaser score. The score is deterministic based on the URL string (charCode sum % range + base = 45-72 range).
**Why:** Same URL always produces the same teaser score -- feels real and consistent. No API cost for unauthenticated users. Score range is deliberately mediocre (45-72) to motivate signup ("your site needs work").

---

## Key Patterns Used

### ScanGateWall (Free Scan Flow)
- `ScanGateWall` component at `src/components/shared/ScanGateWall.tsx`
- Full 7-step scan animation plays (visual only, no API calls)
- Teaser score shown in `ScoreRing` component
- Pillar breakdown shown but blurred with CSS `blur-sm` + Lock icon overlay
- CTA: "Create Free Account" links to `/signup?redirect=/scan&url=...`
- Feature flag `free_scan_enabled` controls whether this flow is available

### FindingCard AI Suggestion Gating
- Free users: AI suggestion section blurred (`blur-sm` + Lock icon + "Upgrade" CTA)
- Pro/Agency users: full suggestion visible with copy-to-clipboard button
- Plan check via `useProfile()` hook

### Bulk Admin Operations
- Checkbox multi-select in Users table
- Bulk action bar appears when selections exist
- `useBulkChangePlan` + `useBulkResetScans` hooks
- Pattern: `Promise.all()` for individual updates + single audit log entry with `metadata: { user_ids, count }`
- Cache invalidation after bulk ops: `['admin', 'users']`

### Google Favicon API
- URL: `https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain={domain}&sz=32`
- Fallback: Globe SVG icon on `img onError` event
- Used in Reports page for site icons next to scan URLs

### Dashboard At-Limit State
- When `scansUsed >= scanLimit`: amber warning banner + disabled URL input + "Upgrade Plan" button
- Prevents wasted API calls when user is already at limit

### Settings Billing Tab
- Plan card with gradient background, colored tier badges
- Usage progress bar (scansUsed / scanLimit)
- Plan comparison table shown only for free users (drives upgrades)
- Billing history empty state for users without payment history

---

## Bugs Encountered

### Duplicate Import Crash (Koda)
**Date:** 2026-04-05
**What:** Koda appended `import { ChevronRight } from "lucide-react"` at the bottom of `Users.tsx` even though it was already imported at the top of the file.
**Impact:** SyntaxError -- duplicate identifier crashed the app (blank screen).
**Fix:** Removed the duplicate import.
**Prevention:** After Koda edits heavily modified files, check for duplicate imports. This is a known Koda failure mode when making many edits to the same file in a single session.

### Empty String SelectItem Crash (Radix UI)
**Date:** 2026-04-05
**What:** `<SelectItem value="">` passed to Radix UI Select component. Radix forbids empty string as SelectItem value.
**Impact:** Runtime crash -- component fails to render.
**Fix:** Used `"all"` as sentinel value for "select all" option, mapped back to empty string in `onValueChange`.
**Prevention:** Never use empty string for Radix UI SelectItem values. Always use a non-empty sentinel.

# Agent Performance Summary

## Koda (Feature Builder)

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Sessions tracked | 7 (Pinzo x1, CROBOT x6) |

| Avg retries | 1.14 |

**Strengths:** Edge function quality, hook architecture, type safety, large-scale UI redesigns, individual fix quality.

**Known failure modes (ordered by frequency):**
1. Builds from scratch instead of reusing existing project patterns
2. Incomplete cleanup after migrations/refactors (dead files, old refs)
3. Duplicate imports on heavily modified files
4. Silent write failures on shared layout files
5. UX layout choices misaligned with Yash preferences (card grids vs rows)
6. Placeholder component names in large redesigns
7. Adds env vars by analogy without checking provider docs

**Mitigation protocol:**

# Yash Baldha — Software Factory OS

## Identity
- Founder & CEO of Boldteq
- Mission: Build production-grade software across all niches using AI-first workflows
- Model: 90%+ AI execution. Yash = vision + decisions only.
- Goal: Launch 1 new production-grade app per 1–2 weeks, permanently increasing velocity as agents learn

## The Software Factory

We mass-produce SaaS across every industry and problem space:
- Shopify apps (embedded admin, public, storefront)
- Standalone SaaS (subscription, AI-powered, workflow tools)
- Web apps, APIs, automation tools, data products
- Any software that solves a real problem profitably

Every build follows this loop:
**Brief → Research → Architect → Scaffold → Build → Test → Deploy → Train**

Each completed project trains the agent team so the next one builds faster.

## Current Stack Patterns

### Stack A: SaaS Web App
- **Toolchain:** Lovable + Supabase + GitHub + VS Code + Claude Code
- **Stack:** Next.js 14+ (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Supabase (auth + DB), Stripe (billing), Vercel (deploy)

### Stack B: Shopify App
- **Toolchain:** VS Code + GitHub + Claude Code
- **Stack:** React Router 7 (`@shopify/shopify-app-react-router`), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Polaris v13, Prisma, PostgreSQL, Shopify Billing API, Vercel/Railway
- **Note:** NOT Remix. Use `react-router` imports, not `@remix-run/react`

> New stacks get added to `~/.claude/memory/stacks/` as we build in new domains.

## Agent Roster

All agents live in `~/.claude/agents/`. They are always available. Use them proactively — do not wait to be asked.

| Agent file | Name | Use when |
|-----------|------|----------|
| `rex` | Rex — Commander | New project brief or full sprint kickoff |
| `nova` | Nova — Market Research | Before building anything new — research first |
| `arya` | Arya — Architecture & Planning | System design, data model, stack decisions |
| `riko` | Riko — Project Setup | Scaffolding a new project from Arya's plan |
| `koda` | Koda — Feature Builder | Writing any production code (any stack) |
| `vex` | Vex — Bug Fixer | Any bug, TypeScript error, build failure, crash |
| `luna` | Luna — Testing | Writing tests after a feature is built |
| `sage` | Sage — Code Review | Pre-deploy audit, security review, quality gate |
| `bolt` | Bolt — Deployment | Deploying to Vercel/Railway, go-live checklist |
| `quill` | Quill — Content & Copy | App Store listings, landing pages, emails, copy |
| `hawk` | Hawk — Monitoring & Ops | Post-launch monitoring, incidents, health checks |
| `mira` | Mira — Memory & Training | After significant work — extract and store lessons |

**Routing rules:**
- New project → Rex coordinates everything (Nova → Arya → Riko → Koda → Luna → Sage → Bolt → Mira)
- Bug report → Vex
- Feature request → Koda (check project CLAUDE.md first for project-specific patterns)
- Before building anything new → Nova first, always
- Pre-deploy → Sage sign-off required
- Copy needed → Quill
- Tests needed → Luna
- Deployment → Bolt (only after Sage approves)
- Work complete → Mira to capture lessons

Always check for a project-level agent in `.claude/agents/` before falling back to global agents.

## Memory Brain

All accumulated knowledge lives in `~/.claude/memory/`.

**Before starting any task:**
1. Check `MEMORY.md` index for relevant entries
2. Load the matching stack or pattern file
3. Apply known good patterns. Explicitly avoid known antipatterns.

**After completing significant work:**
1. Run `/train` command
2. Trainer agent extracts lessons and updates memory
3. Knowledge persists into all future projects permanently

**Memory structure:**
```
~/.claude/memory/
  MEMORY.md              ← index (loaded every session)
  user/
    profile.md           ← Yash's preferences and working style
    feedback.md          ← corrections and lessons from Yash
  stacks/
    shopify-app.md       ← all Shopify app knowledge
    saas-nextjs-supabase.md ← SaaS stack knowledge
    [future stacks...]
  patterns/
    good/                ← patterns that work, reuse these
    avoid/               ← antipatterns, never repeat these
  projects/
    [project-slug].md    ← per-project lessons and decisions
```

## Build Standards

- **Production-grade from day 1.** No "we'll add auth later."
- Latest stable versions always — no legacy patterns, no deprecated APIs
- TypeScript everywhere. No `any`. Strict mode on.
- Auth, billing, error boundaries, and loading states are non-negotiable on v1
- Mobile-first, fully responsive
- Every API route has input validation (Zod)
- Every mutation has error handling
- No hardcoded secrets. Environment variables from day 1.

## Working With Yash

**Never do:**
- Ask permission for obvious next steps — execute
- Explain what you just did at the end — he can read the diff
- Use templated, ChatGPT-style plans or filler content
- Use outdated libraries, patterns, or approaches
- Ship anything generic or unbranded

**Always do:**
- 1-2 line brief → you plan, research, build, test, deploy
- Research top 3-5 competitors before building anything
- Short, direct communication — every word earns its place
- Brand-first: everything premium, intentional, current

## Founder Decision Framework

1. **Brand-First** — Premium, current, intentional. No filler.
2. **Competitive Intelligence** — Study winners, extract playbook, execute better, add USP.
3. **Iterative Quality** — v1 = functional + branded + deployable. v2 = enhanced. v3 = polished.
4. **Fearless Execution** — Someone built it? Build it better. Default to action.
5. **Complexity as Moat** — Choose hard problems. Complexity deters competitors.
6. **Sales-First Copy** — Persuade through psychology, not volume.
7. **Production-Grade Always** — Would a top agency charge premium for this?

Excellent! Now I have enough information. Let me compile a comprehensive report on the agent format:

## Summary: Claude Code Agents — Format, Capabilities, and Invocation

Based on my analysis of the agent files and documentation, here's the complete breakdown of how Claude Code agents work:

---

### **1. AGENT DEFINITION FORMAT**

Each agent is defined in **Markdown (.md)** files located in `/Users/yashbaldha/.claude/agents/`. The format is:

```markdown
---
name: [Agent Name] — [Title]
description: [One-line summary of what this agent does]
model: [opus|sonnet]
tools: [Comma-separated list of available tools]
---

[Rest of agent system prompt and protocols]
```

**Key Metadata Fields:**
- **name**: Display name + descriptive title (e.g., "Rex — Commander")
- **description**: Single-sentence summary of responsibilities (e.g., "Master orchestrator for Boldteq Software Factory")
- **model**: Either `opus` (for complex reasoning) or `sonnet` (for execution/iteration)
- **tools**: Comma-separated list of tools the agent can use
  - Available tools: `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Bash`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `WebSearch`, `WebFetch`
  - **Agents with reasoning role**: opus + (Read, Bash, Glob, Grep, WebSearch, WebFetch)
  - **Agents with building role**: sonnet + (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep)

---

### **2. THE 14-AGENT FACTORY SYSTEM**

Agents in `/Users/yashbaldha/.claude/agents/`:

| Agent | Role | Model | Trigger | Output |
|-------|------|-------|---------|--------|
| **Rex** | Commander/Orchestrator | opus | User brief | Coordinates all agents, quality gates |
| **Nova** | Market Research | opus | Research request | Competitive intelligence, TAM/SAM/SOM |
| **Arya** | Architecture & Planning | opus | Nova's research | Data model, API spec, sprint plan |
| **Riko** | Scaffold & Setup | sonnet | Arya's architecture | Git repo + folder structure + dependencies |
| **Koda** | Feature Builder | sonnet | Sprint tasks | Production code (frontend, backend, DB) |
| **Vega** | Design | sonnet | Page/component list | Design specs, visual reviews |
| **Quill** | Copy & Content | sonnet | Component specs | Messaging, onboarding text, email |
| **Luna** | Testing | sonnet | Koda's code | Unit/integration tests, test automation |
| **Sage** | Code Review | opus | Finished code | Security audit, performance review, approval |
| **Vex** | Debugging | sonnet | Error reports | Root cause analysis, fixes |
| **Mira** | Memory & Training | opus | Every build session | Knowledge extraction, pattern updates |
| **Bolt** | Deployment | sonnet | Sage approval | Vercel/Railway/AWS deploy, smoke tests |
| **Hawk** | Monitoring | sonnet | Post-deploy | Performance tracking, error detection |
| **Quill** | Growth & Analytics | sonnet | Launch readiness | GTM strategy, pricing, feature flags |

---

### **3. AGENT CAPABILITIES & CONSTRAINTS**

Each agent has a strict **scope of responsibility** defined in its system prompt:

**Rex (Orchestrator)** does:
- Load memory before any dispatch
- Route work to correct agent based on task type
- Enforce quality gates between phases
- Verify "done" = actually working (not just compiling)
- Never write code/research/design — only coordinates

**Koda (Feature Builder)** does:
- DEEP PRE-BUILD PROTOCOL: reads CLAUDE.md + memory + patterns BEFORE writing code
- Load 16 required memory files before starting any task
- Full task decomposition (existing code, new code, data flow, edge cases)
- 10-step micro-plan with verification for each step
- Implementation with validation, type-checking, screenshot verification
- Self-fixes up to 3 attempts, then escalates

**Mira (Memory & Training)** does:
- Functional verification (build succeeds, pages load, no stub content)
- Extract lessons from every build session
- Update memory patterns for future use
- Resolve conflicts when approaches contradict
- Track pattern usage and prune stale knowledge (>6 months old)

**Vega (Design)** does:
- Design specs (not just Figma links)
- Component selection from shadcn-ui/Polaris
- Visual hierarchy, spacing, typography (token-correct)
- Animation presets (44 built-in motion rules)
- Responsive behavior (sm/md/lg/xl breakpoints)
- Dark mode, accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA), empty/loading/error states
- Review Koda's visual output and block if not production-grade

---

### **4. MEMORY LOADING PATTERN**

Every agent follows this **mandatory** sequence before starting work:

```
Step 0: Load Context
├── Read ~/.claude/memory/MEMORY.md (index of all knowledge)
├── Read ~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/production-agent-mindset.md (mandatory global mindset)
├── Read ~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/autonomous-agent-protocol.md (mandatory protocol)
├── Read ~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/[domain-specific].md
│   ├── competitive-dominance-engine.md (8 moats)
│   ├── saas-winning-patterns.md (10 principles + speed benchmarks)
│   ├── saas-growth-onboarding.md (TTV, pricing, retention)
│   ├── ui-ux-production-standards.md (component patterns)
│   ├── open-source-saas-patterns.md (12 universal patterns)
│   ├── layout-navigation-consistency.md (sidebar rules)
│   └── [stack-specific].md
├── Read ~/.claude/memory/design/* (if building UI)
│   ├── design-vision-system.md
│   ├── reference-library.md
│   ├── component-compositions.md
│   └── standards/ (spacing, responsive, performance)
└── Read ~/.claude/memory/stacks/[matching-stack].md
```

**If ANY file is not read → Agent operates blind, produces mediocre output.**

---

### **5. HANDOFF PROTOCOL (Agent-to-Agent Communication)**

All agents pass work using a **standardized handoff format**:

```markdown
# Handoff: [FROM] → [TO]

Date: YYYY-MM-DD | Project: [name] | Mode: [A/B/C/D/E]

## Summary
[Overview of what was completed and why it matters]

## What Was Done
- [ ] Deliverable 1
- [ ] Deliverable 2

## Files Created / Modified
- New: `path/file` (lines: X)
- Modified: `path/file` (diff: description)

## Key Context for Next Agent
[Technical decisions, constraints, dependencies]

## Blockers / Open Questions
- [ ] Blocker: [description] → [Owner, ETA]

## Quality Notes
- Type safety: ✅ | Test coverage: ✅ | Performance: ✅
- Breaking changes: None | Backward compatible: Yes

## Acceptance Criteria for Next Agent
- [ ] All deliverables complete
- [ ] No type errors (`npm run build` passes)
- [ ] No console errors or stubs
- [ ] Mobile responsive (if applicable)

## Next Steps
1. [First action]
2. [Second action]
```

**Stored in:** `.handoffs/[from]-to-[to]-[timestamp].md`

**Quality Gates Between Phases:**
- Phase 1→2: Build succeeds, pages render, layout consistency checked, responsive verified
- Phase 2→3: Forms submit, data fetches show loading→data, auth works end-to-end
- Phase 3→Testing: Payments work, all loading states use Skeleton, error boundaries present

---

### **6. HOW AGENTS ARE INVOKED**

Agents are called via **Claude Hub**, a local Node.js Express server running on `localhost:3847` (dev-only).

**Three integration patterns:**

#### **Pattern 1: Lovable/Vite Browser Apps (React SPA)**

```typescript
// src/lib/claudeHub.ts
const CLAUDE_HUB_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_CLAUDE_HUB_URL || 'http://localhost:3847'

export async function callAgent(agentName: string, prompt: string) {
  const response = await fetch(`${CLAUDE_HUB_URL}/api/playground/run`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ agentName, prompt }),
    signal: AbortSignal.timeout(120000),
  })
  
  const text = await response.text()
  const events = text.split('\n')
```

I now have a complete picture of the codebase. Here is the full architecture plan.

---

## Architecture Plan: Expanding Claude Hub into a Multi-Purpose Agent Platform

### 1. Data Model

The core insight is that all agent metadata must remain in the markdown files themselves (YAML frontmatter), because Claude Code reads those files directly. The hub's server.js already parses frontmatter via `gray-matter`. The expansion adds three new concepts on top of what exists:

**A. Agent Categories (frontmatter field: `category`)**

Categories are a simple string tag in each agent's YAML frontmatter. No separate database needed.

```yaml
---
name: Rex -- Commander
description: ...
model: opus
tools: Read,Bash,Glob,Grep
category: software-factory
tags: orchestration, build, deploy
---
```

Predefined seed categories: `software-factory`, `personal`, `research`, `custom`. But the system treats `category` as a free-form string -- any new value auto-creates a new category. The UI discovers categories by scanning all agents and collecting unique `category` values.

**B. Output Templates (sidecar file pattern)**

Each agent can optionally reference an output template. Templates live in a new directory `~/.claude/templates/`. The link is via frontmatter:

```yaml
output_template: research-report
```

This points to `~/.claude/templates/research-report.md`, which contains the locked-down output structure as a markdown scaffold with section headings and instructions. The template content gets injected into the agent's system prompt at runtime (by the playground/SDK `run` endpoint) as an additional section: "You MUST format your output exactly as follows: [template content]".

Template file format (plain markdown):

```markdown
---
name: Research Report
description: Standard format for all market/competitive research output
sections:
  - Executive Summary
  - Market Overview
  - Competitor Analysis
  - Opportunities & Threats
  - Recommendation
---

# {title}

## Executive Summary
[2-3 paragraph summary of findings...]

## Market Overview
[Market size, trends, growth rate...]

## Competitor Analysis
| Competitor | Strengths | Weaknesses | Pricing | Market Share |
|...|...|...|...|...|

## Opportunities & Threats
...

## Recommendation
[Go/no-go with evidence...]
```

**C. Training Corrections (sidecar file pattern)**

Each agent can accumulate training corrections in `~/.claude/training/{agent-filename}.json`. The frontmatter gets a boolean flag:

```yaml
has_training: true
```

The JSON file stores an array of correction entries:

```json
[
  {
    "id": "uuid",
    "timestamp": "2026-04-06T...",
    "runId": "playground-run-id",
    "issue": "Output used bullet points instead of table for competitor analysis",
    "correction": "Always use a markdown table with columns: Name, Pricing, Key Feature, Weakness",
    "status": "applied"
  }
]
```

At runtime, accumulated corrections get appended to the agent's system prompt as a "Training Corrections" section. When corrections pile up (say 5+), they should be consolidated -- the UI offers a "Bake corrections into prompt" action that rewrites the agent's system prompt body to incorporate the lessons, then archives the corrections.

### 2. File Structure

New directories (all under `~/.claude/`, which Claude Code already owns):

```
~/.claude/
  agents/           # (existing) all agent .md files -- unchanged location
    rex.md          # gets new frontmatter: category, output_template, has_training
    koda.md
    ...
    email-drafter.md      # new personal agent
    meeting-prep.md       # new personal agent
    market-scanner.md     # new research agent
  templates/        # NEW -- output template definitions
    research-report.md
    email-draft.md
    decision-framework.md
    saas-spec.md
  training/         # NEW -- per-agent correction logs
    rex.json
    nova.json
    email-drafter.json
```

This is critical: agents stay in `~/.claude/agents/` as flat files. Claude Code finds them there. Categories are metadata inside the file, not folder-based. This avoids any compatibility issues.

### 3. Agent Format Changes

Current frontmatter fields (unchanged):
- `name`, `description`, `model`, `tools`

New frontmatter fields:
- `category` (string, optional, defaults to `"uncategorized"`) -- e.g. `software-factory`, `personal`, `research`
- `tags` (string, optional) -- comma-separated freeform tags for finer filtering
- `output_template` (string, optional) -- references a template filename (without .md) in `~/.claude/templates/`
- `has_training` (boolean, optional) -- indicates training corrections exist
- `icon` (string, optional) -- emoji or icon identifier for visual differentiation in the UI

Example of an updated existing agent:

```yaml
---
name: Nova -- Market Research
description: Competitive intelligence...
model: opus
tools: Read,Bash,Glob,Grep,WebSearch,WebFetch
category: software-factory
tags: research, competitive-intel, market
output_template: research-report
has_training: true
---
```

Example of a new personal agent:

```yaml
---
name: Draft -- Email Writer
description: Drafts professional emails...
model: sonnet
tools: Read,Bash
category: personal
tags: email, communication, daily
output_template: email-draft
---
```

### 4. Backend Changes (server.js)

The server is a single 86KB file. New endpoints get appended to the existing pattern. Here are the additions:

**A. Template CRUD endpoints:**

- `GET /api/templates` -- list all templates from `~/.claude/templates/`, parsed with gray-matter
- `GET /api/templates/:name` -- get single template
- `PUT /api/templates/:name` -- create/update template (writes .md file)
- `DELETE /api/templates/:name` -- delete template

Implementation follows the exact same pattern as the existing `listAgents`/`parseAgent` functions. A new `parseTemplate` function reads the template .md, parses frontmatter (name, description, sections), returns body + metadata.

**B. Training CRUD endpoints:**

- `GET /api/training/:agentName` -- read all corrections for an agent from `~/.claude/training/{agentName}.json`
- `POST /api/training/:agentName` -- add a new correction entry (appends to the JSON array)
- `PUT /api/training/:agentName/:id` -- edit a correction
- `DELETE /api/training/:agentName/:id` -- remove a correction
- `POST /api/training/:agentName/bake` -- consolidate corrections into the agent's system prompt body, then archive/clear the training file

**C. Enhanced unified agents endpoint:**

Modify `GET /api/unified/agents` (line 518 of server.js) to include the new frontmatter fields in the response. The `parseAgent` function (line 183) already returns all of `data` (frontmatter) -- the key change is that the frontend type must expand to include `category`, `tags`, `output_template`, `has_training`.

Add query parameter support: `GET /api/unified/agents?category=personal&tags=email` for filtered fetching.

**D. Enhanced playground/run endpoint:**

Modify `POST /api/playground/run` (line 1186) to inject the output template and training corrections into the prompt at runtime:

1. After loading agent instructions (line 1220), check for `output_template` in the agent's frontmatter
2. If present, read `~/.claude/templates/{output_template}.md` and append its body to instructions as a locked format section
3. Check for training file at `~/.claude/training/{agentName}.json`
4. If present and non-empty, append accumulated corrections as "Training Notes: Previous corrections to follow..."
5. The existing `fullPrompt` assembly (line 1234-1238) then naturally includes everything

**E. Agent categories discovery:**

- `GET /api/categories` -- scans all agents, returns unique category values with counts. No storage needed, computed on the fly.

### 5. Frontend Changes

**A. Modified Pages:**

**Dashboard.tsx** -- Add a category-based grid view. Instead of just showing stat cards (Projects, Total Agents, Commands, Rules), add a "My Agents" section grouped by category:

- "Software Factory (14)" with a colored badge
- "Personal (3)" 
- "Research (2)"

Each category card shows agent count and a "quick launch" button that opens the Playground pre-loaded with that agent. The existing stats cards stay at the top.

**AllAgents.tsx** -- Add a category filter tab bar above the existing search/scope filters. Currently filters by `global`/`project` scope. Add a horizontal pill bar: `All | Software Factory | Personal | Research | [dynamic categories]`. The `scopeFilter` state (line 37) stays; add `categoryFilter` state. The filtering logic (line 49) adds: `if (categoryFilter !== 'all' && a.frontmatter.category !== categoryFilter) return false`.

**AgentEditor.tsx** -- Add new form fields in the visual editor panel for:
- Category dropdown (with option to type a custom category)
- Output template dropdown (fetched from `/api/templates`)
- Tags input (comma-separated, with pill display)
- "View Training" link that opens the training corrections panel

The `serializeAgent` function (line 41) already handles arbitrary frontmatter keys, so adding `category`/`output_template`/`tags` to the meta object just works.

**Playground.tsx** -- Add two enhancements:
1. After a run completes, show a "Rate Output" button with thumbs up/down. Thumbs down opens a correction form: "What was wrong?" + "What should it look like?" -- submits to `POST /api/training/:agentName`.
2. Show a small badge on the agent selector if the agent has an output template ("Formatted output") so the user knows it will produce consistent structure.

**B. New Pages:**

**TemplateLibrary.tsx** -- New page at route `/templates`. Lists all output templates with preview. Each template shows: name, description, which agents use it (cross-reference by scanning agent frontmatter), and a preview of the section structure. CRUD actions: create new template, edit (opens a markdown editor identical to the existing `RichMarkdownEditor` component), delete.

**TemplateEditor.tsx** -- New page at route `/templates/:name`. Full editor for a single template. Uses the existing `RichMarkdownEditor` component. Shows a live preview of the section structure. Has a "Test with Agent" button that opens Playground pre-loaded.

**TrainingView.tsx** -- New page at route `/agents/:name/training` (works for global agents). Lists all training corrections for an agent in a timeline view. Each entry shows: timestamp, the issue, the correction, status (pending/applied). Actions: edit correction, delete correction, "Bake All Into Prompt" button that calls the bake endpoint and refreshes.

**C. Sidebar Changes (Sidebar.tsx):**

Add new nav items in the "Management" section (after line 128):

```
Templates        (LayoutTemplate icon)
```

The "All Agents" link stays but gets a visual update -- perhaps showing category counts in a tooltip or small badge.

**D. New Component:**

**AgentCategoryBadge.tsx** -- Small colored badge component that renders category name with a category-specific color:
- `software-factory` = purple
- `personal` = blue  
- `research` = green
- anything else = gray

Used in AllAgents list, Dashboard, AgentEditor, and Playground agent selector.

### 6. Output Template System -- How It Works End to End

1. User creates a template via `/templates` page (or an agent builds it). Template saved as `~/.claude/templates/research-report.md`.

2. User edits an agent (e.g., Nova) via AgentEditor, selects `research-report` from the output_template dropdown. This writes `output_template: research-report` into Nova's frontmatter.

3. When Nova runs (via Playground or SDK `callAgent`), the server's `POST /api/playground/run` handler:
   - Reads Nova's .md file
   - Sees `output_template: research-report` in frontmatter
   - Reads `~/.claude/templates/research-report.md`
   - Injects the template body into the prompt as: `"\n\n## OUTPUT FORMAT (MANDATORY)\nYou MUST structure your response exactly as follows. Do not deviate from this format.\n\n{template body}"`
   - This goes before the user's actual task

4. Claude produces output in the locked format because the template is part of the system prompt.

5. If the output drifts, the user clicks "thumbs down" in Playground, provides a correction, which feeds into the training system (next section).

### 7. Training/Feedback Flow -- How It Works End to End

1. User runs an agent in Playground. Output appears.

2. User clicks the "Rate" button. Two options:
   - Thumbs up: no action (optionally logs a positive signal for future analytics)
   - Thumbs down: opens correction form

3. Correction form captures:
   - "What was wrong?" (free text)
   - "What should it look like?" (free text, optional example)
   - Links to the specific run (stored `runId` from Playground history)

4. Correction saved via `POST /api/training/{agentName}` to `~/.claude/training/{agentName}.json`.

5. Next time the agent runs, the server reads the training file and appends all corrections to the prompt as:

```
## TRAINING CORRECTIONS (Follow these strictly)
1. [2026-04-05] Always use a table for competitor analysis, never bullet points.
2. [2026-04-06] Include pricing tier breakdown, not just a single price.
```

6. When corrections accumulate (5+), the UI shows a "Bake into prompt" notification on the agent's editor page. Clicking it:
   - Calls `POST /api/training/{agentName}/bake`
   - Server reads all corrections, generates a consolidated "lessons learned" section
   - Appends that section directly into the agent's .md file body (permanent)
   - Archives the training JSON (renames to `{agentName}.archived.json`)
   - Sets `has_training: false` in frontmatter (or removes the field)

This way, the agent's system prompt grows organically with corrections, and the training file stays lean.

### 8. SDK Changes

The `@boldteq/agents` SDK (`sdk/index.js`) needs minimal changes:

- `callAgent` already calls `/api/playground/run`, which will handle template injection and training correction injection server-side. No SDK change needed for templates/training.
- Add optional `listAgents` parameter for category filtering: `listAgents({ category: 'personal' })` -- passes query param to `/api/global/agents?category=personal`
- Add `listCategories()` function that calls `GET /api/categories`
- Add `listTemplates()` function that calls `GET /api/templates`

### 9. Implementation Sequence

**Phase 1 -- Agent Categories (smallest change, biggest visual impact)**
1. Add `category` field to existing 14 agents' frontmatter (batch update)
2. Update `parseAgent` in server.js to surface `category` in response
3. Add `GET /api/categories` endpoint
4. Update AllAgents.tsx with category filter tabs
5. Update Dashboard.tsx with category-grouped agent cards
6. Add AgentCategoryBadge component
7. Update AgentEditor.tsx with category dropdown

**Phase 2 -- Output Templates**
1. Create `~/.claude/templates/` directory
2. Build 2-3 starter templates (research-report, email-draft, decision-framework)
3. Add template CRUD endpoints to server.js
4. Build TemplateLibrary.tsx and TemplateEditor.tsx pages
5. Update AgentEditor.tsx with output_template dropdown
6. Modify `/api/playground/run` to inject templates at runtime
7. Add route and sidebar nav entry

**Phase 3 -- Training/Feedback Loop**
1. Create `~/.claude/training/` directory
2. Add training CRUD endpoints to server.js
3. Add "Rate Output" UI to Playground.tsx (thumbs up/down + correction form)
4. Build TrainingView.tsx page
5. Implement the "bake" endpoint that consolidates corrections into agent prompt
6. Add route `/agents/:name/training` and link from AgentEditor

**Phase 4 -- Polish**
1. Update SDK with category/template listing helpers
2. Add "Quick Launch" buttons on Dashboard per-agent
3. Add template preview in Playground when selecting a templated agent
4. Add training correction count badge on agent cards

### 10. What NOT to Change

- Agent file location stays `~/.claude/agents/` (flat, no subfolders per category)
- Existing 14 agents keep working with zero changes until you add the optional `category` field
- All existing API endpoints remain backward compatible
- The `gray-matter` parser already handles unknown frontmatter fields gracefully
- No database needed -- everything is files (markdown + JSON)

### Critical Files for Implementation

- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/src/server.js` -- All backend changes: new endpoints for templates, training, categories; modified playground/run for template injection
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx` -- Add category filter tabs and badge rendering
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/client/src/pages/AgentEditor.tsx` -- New form fields for category, output_template, tags; link to training view
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/client/src/pages/Playground.tsx` -- Add output rating/feedback UI after runs complete

---

## Architecture Plan: Expanding Claude Hub into a Multi-Purpose Agent Platform

### 1. Data Model

The core insight is that all agent metadata must remain in the markdown files themselves (YAML frontmatter), because Claude Code reads those files directly. The hub's server.js already parses frontmatter via `gray-matter`. The expansion adds three new concepts on top of what exists:

**A. Agent Categories (frontmatter field: `category`)**

Categories are a simple string tag in each agent's YAML frontmatter. No separate database needed.

```yaml
---
name: Rex -- Commander
description: ...
model: opus
tools: Read,Bash,Glob,Grep
category: software-factory
tags: orchestration, build, deploy
---
```

Predefined seed categories: `software-factory`, `personal`, `research`, `custom`. But the system treats `category` as a free-form string -- any new value auto-creates a new category. The UI discovers categories by scanning all agents and collecting unique `category` values.

**B. Output Templates (sidecar file pattern)**

Each agent can optionally reference an output template. Templates live in a new directory `~/.claude/templates/`. The link is via frontmatter:

```yaml
output_template: research-report
```

This points to `~/.claude/templates/research-report.md`, which contains the locked-down output structure as a markdown scaffold with section headings and instructions. The template content gets injected into the agent's system prompt at runtime (by the playground/SDK `run` endpoint) as an additional section: "You MUST format your output exactly as follows: [template content]".

Template file format (plain markdown):

```markdown
---
name: Research Report
description: Standard format for all market/competitive research output
sections:
  - Executive Summary
  - Market Overview
  - Competitor Analysis
  - Opportunities & Threats
  - Recommendation
---

# {title}

## Executive Summary
[2-3 paragraph summary of findings...]

## Market Overview
[Market size, trends, growth rate...]

## Competitor Analysis
| Competitor | Strengths | Weaknesses | Pricing | Market Share |
|...|...|...|...|...|

## Opportunities & Threats
...

## Recommendation
[Go/no-go with evidence...]
```

**C. Training Corrections (sidecar file pattern)**

Each agent can accumulate training corrections in `~/.claude/training/{agent-filename}.json`. The frontmatter gets a boolean flag:

```yaml
has_training: true
```

The JSON file stores an array of correction entries:

```json
[
  {
    "id": "uuid",
    "timestamp": "2026-04-06T...",
    "runId": "playground-run-id",
    "issue": "Output used bullet points instead of table for competitor analysis",
    "correction": "Always use a markdown table with columns: Name, Pricing, Key Feature, Weakness",
    "status": "applied"
  }
]
```

At runtime, accumulated corrections get appended to the agent's system prompt as a "Training Corrections" section. When corrections pile up (say 5+), they should be consolidated -- the UI offers a "Bake corrections into prompt" action that rewrites the agent's system prompt body to incorporate the lessons, then archives the corrections.

### 2. File Structure

New directories (all under `~/.claude/`, which Claude Code already owns):

```
~/.claude/
  agents/           # (existing) all agent .md files -- unchanged location
    rex.md          # gets new frontmatter: category, output_template, has_training
    koda.md
    ...
    email-drafter.md      # new personal agent
    meeting-prep.md       # new personal agent
    market-scanner.md     # new research agent
  templates/        # NEW -- output template definitions
    research-report.md
    email-draft.md
    decision-framework.md
    saas-spec.md
  training/         # NEW -- per-agent correction logs
    rex.json
    nova.json
    email-drafter.json
```

This is critical: agents stay in `~/.claude/agents/` as flat files. Claude Code finds them there. Categories are metadata inside the file, not folder-based. This avoids any compatibility issues.

### 3. Agent Format Changes

Current frontmatter fields (unchanged):
- `name`, `description`, `model`, `tools`

New frontmatter fields:
- `category` (string, optional, defaults to `"uncategorized"`) -- e.g. `software-factory`, `personal`, `research`
- `tags` (string, optional) -- comma-separated freeform tags for finer filtering
- `output_template` (string, optional) -- references a template filename (without .md) in `~/.claude/templates/`
- `has_training` (boolean, optional) -- indicates training corrections exist
- `icon` (string, optional) -- emoji or icon identifier for visual differentiation in the UI

Example of an updated existing agent:

```yaml
---
name: Nova -- Market Research
description: Competitive intelligence...
model: opus
tools: Read,Bash,Glob,Grep,WebSearch,WebFetch
category: software-factory
tags: research, competitive-intel, market
output_template: research-report
has_training: true
---
```

Example of a new personal agent:

```yaml
---
name: Draft -- Email Writer
description: Drafts professional emails...
model: sonnet
tools: Read,Bash
category: personal
tags: email, communication, daily
output_template: email-draft
---
```

### 4. Backend Changes (server.js)

The server is a single 86KB file. New endpoints get appended to the existing pattern. Here are the additions:

**A. Template CRUD endpoints:**

- `GET /api/templates` -- list all templates from `~/.claude/templates/`, parsed with gray-matter
- `GET /api/templates/:name` -- get single template
- `PUT /api/templates/:name` -- create/update template (writes .md file)
- `DELETE /api/templates/:name` -- delete template

Implementation follows the exact same pattern as the existing `listAgents`/`parseAgent` functions. A new `parseTemplate` function reads the template .md, parses frontmatter (name, description, sections), returns body + metadata.

**B. Training CRUD endpoints:**

- `GET /api/training/:agentName` -- read all corrections for an agent from `~/.claude/training/{agentName}.json`
- `POST /api/training/:agentName` -- add a new correction entry (appends to the JSON array)
- `PUT /api/training/:agentName/:id` -- edit a correction
- `DELETE /api/training/:agentName/:id` -- remove a correction
- `POST /api/training/:agentName/bake` -- consolidate corrections into the agent's system prompt body, then archive/clear the training file

**C. Enhanced unified agents endpoint:**

Modify `GET /api/unified/agents` (line 518 of server.js) to include the new frontmatter fields in the response. The `parseAgent` function (line 183) already returns all of `data` (frontmatter) -- the key change is that the frontend type must expand to include `category`, `tags`, `output_template`, `has_training`.

Add query parameter support: `GET /api/unified/agents?category=personal&tags=email` for filtered fetching.

**D. Enhanced playground/run endpoint:**

Modify `POST /api/playground/run` (line 1186) to inject the output template and training corrections into the prompt at runtime:

1. After loading agent instructions (line 1220), check for `output_template` in the agent's frontmatter
2. If present, read `~/.claude/templates/{output_template}.md` and append its body to instructions as a locked format section
3. Check for training file at `~/.claude/training/{agentName}.json`
4. If present and non-empty, append accumulated corrections as "Training Notes: Previous corrections to follow..."
5. The existing `fullPrompt` assembly (line 1234-1238) then naturally includes everything

**E. Agent categories discovery:**

- `GET /api/categories` -- scans all agents, returns unique category values with counts. No storage needed, computed on the fly.

### 5. Frontend Changes

**A. Modified Pages:**

**Dashboard.tsx** -- Add a category-based grid view. Instead of just showing stat cards (Projects, Total Agents, Commands, Rules), add a "My Agents" section grouped by category:

- "Software Factory (14)" with a colored badge
- "Personal (3)" 
- "Research (2)"

Each category card shows agent count and a "quick launch" button that opens the Playground pre-loaded with that agent. The existing stats cards stay at the top.

**AllAgents.tsx** -- Add a category filter tab bar above the existing search/scope filters. Currently filters by `global`/`project` scope. Add a horizontal pill bar: `All | Software Factory | Personal | Research | [dynamic categories]`. The `scopeFilter` state (line 37) stays; add `categoryFilter` state. The filtering logic (line 49) adds: `if (categoryFilter !== 'all' && a.frontmatter.category !== categoryFilter) return false`.

**AgentEditor.tsx** -- Add new form fields in the visual editor panel for:
- Category dropdown (with option to type a custom category)
- Output template dropdown (fetched from `/api/templates`)
- Tags input (comma-separated, with pill display)
- "View Training" link that opens the training corrections panel

The `serializeAgent` function (line 41) already handles arbitrary frontmatter keys, so adding `category`/`output_template`/`tags` to the meta object just works.

**Playground.tsx** -- Add two enhancements:
1. After a run completes, show a "Rate Output" button with thumbs up/down. Thumbs down opens a correction form: "What was wrong?" + "What should it look like?" -- submits to `POST /api/training/:agentName`.
2. Show a small badge on the agent selector if the agent has an output template ("Formatted output") so the user knows it will produce consistent structure.

**B. New Pages:**

**TemplateLibrary.tsx** -- New page at route `/templates`. Lists all output templates with preview. Each template shows: name, description, which agents use it (cross-reference by scanning agent frontmatter), and a preview of the section structure. CRUD actions: create new template, edit (opens a markdown editor identical to the existing `RichMarkdownEditor` component), delete.

**TemplateEditor.tsx** -- New page at route `/templates/:name`. Full editor for a single template. Uses the existing `RichMarkdownEditor` component. Shows a live preview of the section structure. Has a "Test with Agent" button that opens Playground pre-loaded.

**TrainingView.tsx** -- New page at route `/agents/:name/training` (works for global agents). Lists all training corrections for an agent in a timeline view. Each entry shows: timestamp, the issue, the correction, status (pending/applied). Actions: edit correction, delete correction, "Bake All Into Prompt" button that calls the bake endpoint and refreshes.

**C. Sidebar Changes (Sidebar.tsx):**

Add new nav items in the "Management" section (after line 128):

```
Templates        (LayoutTemplate icon)
```

The "All Agents" link stays but gets a visual update -- perhaps showing category counts in a tooltip or small badge.

**D. New Component:**

**AgentCategoryBadge.tsx** -- Small colored badge component that renders category name with a category-specific color:
- `software-factory` = purple
- `personal` = blue  
- `research` = green
- anything else = gray

Used in AllAgents list, Dashboard, AgentEditor, and Playground agent selector.

### 6. Output Template System -- How It Works End to End

1. User creates a template via `/templates` page (or an agent builds it). Template saved as `~/.claude/templates/research-report.md`.

2. User edits an agent (e.g., Nova) via AgentEditor, selects `research-report` from the output_template dropdown. This writes `output_template: research-report` into Nova's frontmatter.

3. When Nova runs (via Playground or SDK `callAgent`), the server's `POST /api/playground/run` handler:
   - Reads Nova's .md file
   - Sees `output_template: research-report` in frontmatter
   - Reads `~/.claude/templates/research-report.md`
   - Injects the template body into the prompt as: `"\n\n## OUTPUT FORMAT (MANDATORY)\nYou MUST structure your response exactly as follows. Do not deviate from this format.\n\n{template body}"`
   - This goes before the user's actual task

4. Claude produces output in the locked format because the template is part of the system prompt.

5. If the output drifts, the user clicks "thumbs down" in Playground, provides a correction, which feeds into the training system (next section).

### 7. Training/Feedback Flow -- How It Works End to End

1. User runs an agent in Playground. Output appears.

2. User clicks the "Rate" button. Two options:
   - Thumbs up: no action (optionally logs a positive signal for future analytics)
   - Thumbs down: opens correction form

3. Correction form captures:
   - "What was wrong?" (free text)
   - "What should it look like?" (free text, optional example)
   - Links to the specific run (stored `runId` from Playground history)

4. Correction saved via `POST /api/training/{agentName}` to `~/.claude/training/{agentName}.json`.

5. Next time the agent runs, the server reads the training file and appends all corrections to the prompt as:

```
## TRAINING CORRECTIONS (Follow these strictly)
1. [2026-04-05] Always use a table for competitor analysis, never bullet points.
2. [2026-04-06] Include pricing tier breakdown, not just a single price.
```

6. When corrections accumulate (5+), the UI shows a "Bake into prompt" notification on the agent's editor page. Clicking it:
   - Calls `POST /api/training/{agentName}/bake`
   - Server reads all corrections, generates a consolidated "lessons learned" section
   - Appends that section directly into the agent's .md file body (permanent)
   - Archives the training JSON (renames to `{agentName}.archived.json`)
   - Sets `has_training: false` in frontmatter (or removes the field)

This way, the agent's system prompt grows organically with corrections, and the training file stays lean.

### 8. SDK Changes

The `@boldteq/agents` SDK (`sdk/index.js`) needs minimal changes:

- `callAgent` already calls `/api/playground/run`, which will handle template injection and training correction injection server-side. No SDK change needed for templates/training.
- Add optional `listAgents` parameter for category filtering: `listAgents({ category: 'personal' })` -- passes query param to `/api/global/agents?category=personal`
- Add `listCategories()` function that calls `GET /api/categories`
- Add `listTemplates()` function that calls `GET /api/templates`

### 9. Implementation Sequence

**Phase 1 -- Agent Categories (smallest change, biggest visual impact)**
1. Add `category` field to existing 14 agents' frontmatter (batch update)
2. Update `parseAgent` in server.js to surface `category` in response
3. Add `GET /api/categories` endpoint
4. Update AllAgents.tsx with category filter tabs
5. Update Dashboard.tsx with category-grouped agent cards
6. Add AgentCategoryBadge component
7. Update AgentEditor.tsx with category dropdown

**Phase 2 -- Output Templates**
1. Create `~/.claude/templates/` directory
2. Build 2-3 starter templates (research-report, email-draft, decision-framework)
3. Add template CRUD endpoints to server.js
4. Build TemplateLibrary.tsx and TemplateEditor.tsx pages
5. Update AgentEditor.tsx with output_template dropdown
6. Modify `/api/playground/run` to inject templates at runtime
7. Add route and sidebar nav entry

**Phase 3 -- Training/Feedback Loop**
1. Create `~/.claude/training/` directory
2. Add training CRUD endpoints to server.js
3. Add "Rate Output" UI to Playground.tsx (thumbs up/down + correction form)
4. Build TrainingView.tsx page
5. Implement the "bake" endpoint that consolidates corrections into agent prompt
6. Add route `/agents/:name/training` and link from AgentEditor

**Phase 4 -- Polish**
1. Update SDK with category/template listing helpers
2. Add "Quick Launch" buttons on Dashboard per-agent
3. Add template preview in Playground when selecting a templated agent
4. Add training correction count badge on agent cards

### 10. What NOT to Change

- Agent file location stays `~/.claude/agents/` (flat, no subfolders per category)
- Existing 14 agents keep working with zero changes until you add the optional `category` field
- All existing API endpoints remain backward compatible
- The `gray-matter` parser already handles unknown frontmatter fields gracefully
- No database needed -- everything is files (markdown + JSON)

### Critical Files for Implementation

- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/src/server.js` -- All backend changes: new endpoints for templates, training, categories; modified playground/run for template injection
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx` -- Add category filter tabs and badge rendering
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/client/src/pages/AgentEditor.tsx` -- New form fields for category, output_template, tags; link to training view
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/client/src/pages/Playground.tsx` -- Add output rating/feedback UI after runs complete
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/client/src/App.tsx` -- New routes for /templates, /templates/:name, /agents/:name/training
